transcript.text:
Thank you all for being here. As you know, I've received Grandma's 90-by-60-centimeter stained-glass window, and I want to get it displayed in the family home before our autumn gathering. We have three location options — the south-facing breakfast-room window, the west hallway, or the reading room — and we'll need to decide on a protective covering and lighting, either focused spotlights or a diffuse wall wash. Most importantly, the window needs to remain available for family members to view without an appointment.

Before I make any decisions, I'd like to go around the table and hear from each of you — what you know, what you need, and what you can commit to regarding this project. Who'd like to start?

transcript.text: I found a handwritten note in Grandma's recipe box — she wanted the stained-glass window installed in the south-facing breakfast-room window, where morning light would pass through it. I haven't shown it to anyone until now.

transcript.text: I have something important to share. I spoke with conservator Dr. Lena Ortiz about how to properly protect the stained glass. She recommended UV-filtering acrylic with a five-centimeter ventilation gap behind the glass, rather than ordinary glass mounted directly against it. This approach would better preserve the window over time. I haven't had a chance to bring this to the group until now.
